tool_signatures.name: delete_process
tool_signatures.description: Stop and remove one or more AI processes (the temporary ones created by run_process / workspace_run) — the same as [dismiss] in the DevGlow UI. Use it to clean up processes you started once they are no longer needed. Does NOT apply to permanent projects; use delete_project for those. A pane that was showing a deleted process is left empty.

tool_signatures.name: delete_project
tool_signatures.description: Delete a kept (permanent) DevGlow project. Stops the process if running. Does NOT apply to AI processes — use delete_process for those.

id.description: Project id (call list_projects first). Must be a permanent project, not an AI process.

tool_signatures.name: delete_workspace
tool_signatures.description: Delete one or more DevGlow workspaces by id. Removes the arrangement only: the processes that were in it keep running and stay in the sidebar (use delete_process / stop_project for those). The workspace the user is currently in is refused — deleting it would replace their screen. Delete only workspaces you created or the user asked you to remove; list_workspaces first.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Workspace ids from list_workspaces.

tool_signatures.name: get_run_history
tool_signatures.description: Recent finished runs of a project or AI process, newest first, with a summary: how long the command usually takes (median of successful runs), how often it succeeds, and how long it takes to start listening on its port. Use it when the user asks how long a build or script usually takes, whether it has been failing, or what happened on recent runs. Only finished runs are recorded; use get_status for whether it is running now. Commands are shown as recorded, with secret values masked as ***.

id.description: Project or AI process ID (from list_projects)

limit.description: How many recent runs to list (default 10, max 50).

tool_signatures.name: list_workspaces
tool_signatures.description: List DevGlow workspaces: id, name, which one the user is in, and the processes placed in each with their running state. Use it before delete_workspace, and to find workspaces left over from earlier work — one whose processes are all stopped or gone is a likely leftover. It cannot tell you who made a workspace; the user arranges them by hand too.

tool_signatures.name: workspace_run
tool_signatures.description: Start two or more processes and arrange them on screen together in a new DevGlow workspace. PREFER this over repeated run_process calls whenever you are starting more than one process — the user does not have to ask to see them. Repeated run_process calls leave each process sitting in the sidebar until the user clicks it into a pane, so starting three that way makes the app look like nothing happened. Each process here starts exactly as run_process would. Always creates a new workspace: a name that already exists gets a numbered variant, and no existing workspace is ever modified, so a repeat call cannot disturb the user
